accepted.name: ethereum_transactions_normalized
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "hash" AS hash,
  "nonce" AS nonce,
  "transaction_index" AS transaction_index,
  "from_address" AS from_address,
  "to_address" AS to_address,
  "value" AS value_wei,
  "gas" AS gas_limit,
  "gas_price" AS gas_price,
  "input" AS input,
  "receipt_cumulative_gas_used" AS receipt_cumulative_gas_used,
  "receipt_gas_used" AS receipt_gas_used,
  "receipt_contract_address" AS receipt_contract_address,
  "receipt_status" AS receipt_status,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  "transaction_type" AS transaction_type,
  "receipt_effective_gas_price" AS receipt_effective_gas_price
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS
accepted.description: Normalized projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS with clean aliases and canonical timestamp/amount columns. Use this when you need a stable, downstream-friendly transactions relation for joins, aggregations, or time-series analyses. | Use for: Transaction volume/time-series for Ethereum; Join transactions to logs/traces/contracts; Compute gas usage or success rates per block or sender

accepted.name: ethereum_token_transfers_normalized
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "token_address" AS token_address,
  "from_address" AS from_address,
  "to_address" AS to_address,
  "value" AS value_raw,
  "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
  "log_index" AS log_index,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS
grain: token_address, transaction_hash, log_index (one row per token transfer event)
accepted.description: Normalized projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TOKEN_TRANSFERS with clean aliases exposing token, from/to, value, and block context. Use for token flow analysis, holder cohorts, and join to transactions/logs. | Use for: Token transfer volume by token or address; On-chain token holder flows and cohorts; Combine with transactions to compute ETH costs per transfer

accepted.name: ethereum_logs_normalized
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "log_index" AS log_index,
  "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
  "transaction_index" AS transaction_index,
  "address" AS contract_address,
  "data" AS data,
  "topics" AS topics,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.LOGS
grain: transaction_hash, log_index (one row per log topic entry)
accepted.description: Normalized projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.LOGS with canonical aliases for event-level analysis and joins into token transfers / contracts. | Use for: Decode events by contract address; Join logs to token_transfers by transaction_hash and log_index; Event frequency/time-series for a contract

accepted.name: ethereum_top_transactions_by_gas_ranked
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.hash AS hash,
  t.block_number AS block_number,
  t.block_timestamp AS block_timestamp,
  t.from_address AS from_address,
  t.to_address AS to_address,
  t.receipt_gas_used AS gas_used,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.block_number ORDER BY t.receipt_gas_used DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_within_block
FROM (
  SELECT
    "hash" AS hash,
    "block_number" AS block_number,
    "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
    "from_address" AS from_address,
    "to_address" AS to_address,
    "receipt_gas_used" AS receipt_gas_used
  FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.TRANSACTIONS
) t
grain: hash (one row per Ethereum transaction, ranked within its block)
accepted.description: Per-block ranking of Ethereum transactions by gas used. Exposes a per-block rank so downstream queries can select top-K gas-consuming transactions per block by filtering on rank. Use when you need top-N txs per block or to annotate transactions with their relative gas cost. | Use for: Select top-N gas-consuming transactions per block; Analyze high-cost transactions over time; Identify outlier transactions by gas within blocks

accepted.name: bitcoin_transactions_denormalized
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  tx."hash" AS hash,
  tx."block_number" AS block_number,
  blk."timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  blk."hash" AS block_hash,
  tx."input_value" AS input_value,
  tx."output_value" AS output_value,
  tx."fee" AS fee,
  tx."is_coinbase" AS is_coinbase,
  tx."input_count" AS input_count,
  tx."output_count" AS output_count
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.TRANSACTIONS tx
LEFT JOIN CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.BLOCKS blk
  ON tx."block_number" = blk."number"
grain: hash (one row per Bitcoin transaction, enriched with block context)
accepted.description: Denormalized join of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.TRANSACTIONS with BLOCKS to expose block-level context for each Bitcoin transaction. Use for block-aware transaction analytics (per-block aggregation, timestamp lookups). | Use for: Bitcoin transaction volume per block or time window; Fee analysis and median fee per block; Coinbase transaction identification and analysis

accepted.name: bitcoin_utxo_flat_outputs
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "index" AS output_index,
  value AS value,
  "type" AS type,
  addr.value::STRING AS address
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS,
LATERAL FLATTEN(input => "addresses") addr
grain: transaction_hash, output_index, address (one row per output address per output)
accepted.description: Flattened projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.OUTPUTS exposing addresses (exploded), value and block context. Useful for UTXO-level analysis, address balance approximations (needs careful spent-checking), and joins with inputs to detect spends. | Use for: Compute funds received by an address (gross inflows); UTXO set scanning and per-address outputs over time; Join outputs to inputs to identify spend events

accepted.name: bitcoin_inputs_flat_spends
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "transaction_hash" AS transaction_hash,
  "block_hash" AS block_hash,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "index" AS input_index,
  "spent_transaction_hash" AS spent_transaction_hash,
  "spent_output_index" AS spent_output_index,
  value AS value,
  "type" AS type,
  addr.value::STRING AS address
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.INPUTS,
LATERAL FLATTEN(input => "addresses") addr
grain: transaction_hash, input_index, address (one row per input address per input)
accepted.description: Flattened projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BITCOIN.INPUTS exposing input addresses, referenced spent outputs, and value. Use for constructing spend graphs and linking outputs to inputs. | Use for: Link outputs to inputs to detect spend chains; Per-address spending behavior and outflows; UTXO lifecycle analysis

accepted.name: band_oracle_requests_flat
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "oracle_request_id" AS oracle_request_id,
  "block_height" AS block_height,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_timestamp_truncated" AS block_timestamp_truncated,
  "request" AS request,
  "reports" AS reports,
  "result" AS result,
  "decoded_result" AS decoded_result,
  "oracle_script" AS oracle_script
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS
accepted.description: Normalized projection of CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.ORACLE_REQUESTS exposing request id, block context and JSON-parsed high-level fields. Use when analyzing oracle request frequency, results, and reports. VARIANT fields are preserved for downstream parsing. | Use for: Count oracle requests over time; Analyze oracle decoded_result distribution; Join oracle requests to block metadata or messages

accepted.name: band_messages_report_events
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."txhash" AS txhash,
  m."block_height" AS block_height,
  m."block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  msg.value:report_id::NUMBER AS report_id,
  rpt.value:reporter::STRING AS reporter,
  rpt.value:answer::STRING AS answer
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.MESSAGES m,
LATERAL FLATTEN(input => m."oracle_Report") msg,
LATERAL FLATTEN(input => msg.value:reports) rpt
grain: txhash, report_id, reporter (one row per report entry within an oracle_Report message)
accepted.description: Extracts and reshapes oracle_Report messages from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_BAND.MESSAGES by unnesting VARIANT report structures into one row per (message) reporter/report entry. Useful when you need to analyze individual report submissions across messages. | Use for: Analyze individual oracle reporter answers; Aggregate reporter activity or disagreement across requests; Join reports back to oracle_requests by report_id

accepted.name: ethereum_contracts_latest
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "address" AS address,
  "bytecode" AS bytecode,
  "function_sighashes" AS function_sighashes,
  "is_erc20" AS is_erc20,
  "is_erc721" AS is_erc721,
  "block_timestamp" AS block_timestamp,
  "block_number" AS block_number,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY "address" ORDER BY "block_number" DESC, "block_timestamp" DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn
FROM CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS
grain: address, ranked rows (one row per contract version observation; pick rn = 1 for latest)
accepted.description: Latest-observed row per contract address from CRYPTO.CRYPTO_ETHEREUM.CONTRACTS using block_number ordering. Exposes a rank so downstream queries can pick latest per address. Use when you need the most recent contract metadata (is_erc20, is_erc721). | Use for: Get latest token classification per contract address; Join latest contract attributes to token transfers or logs
